handbookNote: Alabama Driver Manual, published by the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) Driver License Division, November 2024 edition -- official PDF at alea.gov/sites/default/files/ALEA%20DL%20Manual.pdf, linked from the official manuals page alea.gov/dps/driver-license/driver-license-manuals. Full 92-page text was extracted directly from this PDF and used as the sole grounding source for every question in this bank; no invented facts, no generic driving trivia not actually in the manual. Exam mechanics: the manual itself confirms only a $5.00 knowledge-test fee and states the test 'contains questions on Alabama traffic laws, road signs, and rules of safe driving' drawn from the manual -- it does not publish an official item count, passing score, or time limit, and none was found on alea.gov's driver-license pages after direct search. Five independent third-party DMV test-prep sites (driving-tests.org, driversprep.com, permittest.com, dmv-permit-test.com, dmv-written-test.com) independently and consistently report 30 questions with an 80 percent (24/30 correct) passing score for Alabama's standard Class D knowledge test, and none of them describe the test as timed. Because ALEA does not publish this figure in accessible official text, treat 30 questions / 80 percent passing as well-corroborated by convergent independent sources but not government-confirmed verbatim, and treat the test as untimed absent any stated limit. Content-depth rationale: the manual is substantive (GDL learner/restricted stages, the point system and suspension/revocation/cancellation rules, DUI and BAC penalty tiers, signs/signals/pavement markings/roundabouts, sharing the road with bicycles/motorcycles/large-vehicle No-Zones, freeway interchange types, night/winter/skid/hydroplaning emergencies, and vehicle equipment law) and comfortably supports a large, non-repetitive bank -- 293 questions survive after the build pipeline's exact- and near-duplicate dedup, all traceable to specific manual sections.
